children: Crude oil and refined product futures prices were seeing strong gains to start the week as fighting intensified over the weekend in the Middle East.
U.S. crude prices were up 2.6% at about 11:10 a.m. ET, with the October West Texas Intermediate crude contract climbing by $2.77 to $102.82/bbl and November prices trading $2.30 higher to $98.24/bbl.
Brent crude futures were seeing similar increases, with the November contract climbing by $2.36 to $106.97/bbl and December prices up $2.02 to $101.80/bbl.

Most trading activity in refined products is shifting focus to the next-month contract, with October ULSD futures up by 5.15cts to $5.0108/gal and the more-active November contract climbing by 2.37cts to $4.7920/gal.
October RBOB futures were rising by 6.21cts to $3.3693/gal and November prices were moving 6.33cts higher to $3.1831/gal.

The increases come as markets continue to react to Saudi Arabia's closure on Friday of a pipeline that carries crude to the Red Sea after the pipeline was damaged in attacks. Meanwhile, Houthi fighters in Yemen continue attacking shipping in the Red Sea and made territorial gains over the weekend, allowing them to further threaten sea traffic.

Meanwhile, a meeting planned for Monday involving Iran, Oman and other Persian Gulf countries to discuss future arrangements for shipping through the Strait of Hormuz was canceled, increasing concerns about global energy flows.

U.S. consumers continue to feel the impact of rising petroleum prices, with the U.S. national average price of regular unleaded gasoline rising 0.31ct overnight to $4.3163/gal, its highest since June.
Retail diesel prices continued to set new records, with the national average rising 2.61cts to $6.2301/gal.
